/entries/e_lima/desc: The city where these lives intersect. Church, theatre, mansion and harbor each have their own voices.
/entries/e_lima/archive/0/fields/1/label: The old woman in the street
/entries/e_lima/archive/0/fields/1/text: Residents discuss her clothes, drunkenness and eccentricities, scarcely seeing the care with which she writes
/entries/e_lima/archive/0/fields/2/text: News and favors pass continually among aristocratic parlors, the shore, the convent and the stage
/entries/e_lima/archive/0/fields/3/text: The crowd’s mockery and its later admiration for her letters need not mean that either understands her life
/entries/e_lima/archive/1/title: Familiar, yet hard to return to
/entries/e_lima/archive/1/fields/1/text: Copying plays and music, carrying cargo and running errands make the two quiet men familiar to many in the city
/entries/e_lima/archive/1/fields/2/text: Neighbors care deeply about the brothers’ separation, but cannot thereby carry the survivor through his grief
/entries/e_lima/archive/1/fields/3/text: He keeps leaving and coming back; familiar streets do not immediately recover their former meaning
/entries/e_palace/desc: María’s spacious, splendid house in Lima, which holds the long estrangement between mother and daughter.
/entries/e_palace/archive/0/fields/0/lab: The girl who comes to live here
/entries/e_palace/archive/0/fields/1/tex: The owner reads letters alone here and recognizes a wish for control within her love
/entries/e_palace/archive/0/fields/2/tex: Her long absorption in her private concerns makes it easier for servants to borrow rooms and take belongings
/entries/e_palace/archive/0/fields/3/tex: At times she is deeply kind to the girl, then retreats into her own troubles, leaving the girl’s attachment nowhere to rest
/entries/e_spain/desc: Clara’s home after marriage, and the distant country to which many in Peru keep looking back.
/entries/e_harbor/desc: The shore where travellers and cargo come and go, where mother and daughter part and the brothers work.
/entries/e_harbor/archive/0/fields/1/tex: Tired of copying, the brothers unload ships at the coast, unashamed to work alongside ordinary laborers
/entries/e_harbor/archive/0/fields/2/tex: A voyage means wages and hard work, but also a temporary departure from familiar pain
/entries/e_harbor/archive/0/fields/3/tex: The young man agrees to go, but dies on the return to Lima before boarding the intended ship
/entries/e_convent/desc: Where the abbess cares for orphans and the sick, with laundry troughs, wards and daily expenses to meet.
/entries/e_convent/archive/0/fields/1/te: Care for orphans and the sick, while teaching girls to raise funds, manage affairs and resist injustice
/entries/e_convent/archive/0/fields/2/te: Being expected to succeed her makes a child face adult responsibilities too early
/entries/e_convent/archive/0/fields/3/te: In the mountains Pepita remembers after-supper talk, prayers in the wards and moments of private instruction
/entries/e_convent/archive/1/fields/0/la: What the brothers keep between them
/entries/e_convent/archive/1/fields/1/te: Two abandoned babies are found at the door, then given names, food and stories
/entries/e_convent/archive/1/fields/2/te: The abbess arranges the burial and tries to draw the wandering young man back among other people
/entries/e_convent/archive/1/fields/3/te: Experience and kindness also have limits; at last she must find someone better placed to help
/entries/e_theatre/desc: Where actors and copyists earn their living. Applause onstage often coexists with exacting demands backstage.
/entries/e_theatre/archive/0/fields/1/te: Between two acts of the serious play, the actress leaves her role to sing improvised topical songs
/entries/e_theatre/archive/0/fields/2/te: The actress hears cheers, the girl feels humiliation, and the Marquesa remains absorbed in thoughts of her distant daughter
/entries/e_theatre/archive/0/fields/3/te: Public mockery brings the Viceroy’s intervention and confronts the actress with her conscience during her visit
/entries/e_theatre/archive/1/fields/1/te: An ever-changing repertoire makes learning lines, memorizing and rehearsing prolonged, demanding work
/entries/e_theatre/archive/1/fields/2/te: Teacher and actress know the audience is satisfied, yet still seek the perfection they imagine
/entries/e_theatre/archive/1/fields/3/te: Limited female roles, toil and humiliation wear down her desire; theatrical success need not be her only place to belong
/entries/e_shrine/desc: An Andean place of pilgrimage, surrounded by white walls, bells, a fountain and clear mountain air.
/entries/e_inn/desc: A room on the pilgrimage where two letters with different fates are written, read or torn up.
/entries/e_inn/archive/0/fields/1/text: The girl gives the kitchen particular instructions for porridge, then goes downstairs to check its taste
/entries/e_inn/archive/0/fields/2/text: Pepita appeals for help; the mother learns to write more generously. One letter is torn up, the other preserved
/entries/e_inn/archive/0/fields/3/text: After finishing the letter at dawn, they wait two days before setting out for Lima; they do not die that same morning
/entries/e_room/desc: The brothers’ rented room. Two beds and a copying table witness understanding, estrangement and care.
/entries/e_room/archive/0/fields/0/label: What is repeatedly replaced during illness
/entries/e_room/archive/0/fields/1/text: One takes dictation while the other watches from bed; for the first time the close room holds a feeling they cannot share
/entries/e_room/archive/0/fields/2/text: Cries and curses at night bring complaints, placing the caregiver under pressure from within and outside the room
/entries/e_room/archive/0/fields/3/text: After the death, the survivor refuses to enter the building but keeps returning to its neighborhood
/entries/e_cuzco/desc: Where Esteban works as a copyist after his wanderings, and where the Captain comes to invite him to sea.
/entries/e_court/desc: A center of elaborate etiquette and power, but also of suppers that last until dawn and briefly ease homesickness.
/entries/e_court/archive/0/fields/0/labe: The guest who loves literature and language
/entries/e_court/archive/0/fields/1/text: The Viceroy, Pio and the Captain are at the table; the actress often hurries in after her performance
/entries/e_court/archive/0/fields/2/text: Wars, kings, souls, stars and distant countries offer relief from weariness and homesickness
/entries/e_court/archive/0/fields/3/text: No one wants to leave first, while the exhausted actress has already fallen asleep against her host
/entries/e_garden/desc: A European-style garden in the mountains, where Pio and Camila once spoke beside a bench at dusk.
/entries/e_garden/archive/0/fields/0/lab: The elder of the two visitors
/entries/e_garden/archive/0/fields/1/tex: He hopes for a return to the stage or a journey together; she no longer wants art to determine her whole future
/entries/e_garden/archive/0/fields/2/tex: Pio admits that pride kept him from giving his pupil the praise she deserved
/entries/e_garden/archive/0/fields/3/tex: Her parting kiss on his fingers is real closeness, but does not reverse her refusal to return to the theatre
/entries/e_villa/desc: Camila’s home outside the city. After her illness, its shut doors and windows become a meeting place for care and refusal.
/entries/e_villa/archive/0/title: On either side of the door
/entries/e_villa/archive/0/fields/1/text: She leaves Lima, returns gifts and withdraws into the mountain rooms and estate
/entries/e_villa/archive/0/fields/2/text: After her secret at the mirror is exposed, she expressly forbids Pio to enter even the courtyard
/entries/e_villa/archive/0/fields/3/text: Imitating a girl’s crying draws her downstairs and allows the visitor to circumvent her earlier refusal
/entries/e_bridge/desc: A plant-fiber suspension bridge over the gorge, its thin boards carrying pedestrians. Five different lives meet in an ordinary crossing.
/entries/e_bridge/archive/0/fields/0/lab: The mountain destination in the mother’s story
/entries/e_bridge/archive/0/fields/2/tex: Braided plant-fiber ropes and thin boards carry pedestrians; cargo and animals cross below
/entries/e_bridge/archive/0/fields/3/tex: María and Pepita first cross toward the mountains, returning several days later on their way to Lima
/entries/e_bridge/archive/0/fields/4/tex: Writing anew marks a change, but gives no one foreknowledge of, or protection from, the coming disaster
/entries/e_bridge/archive/1/fields/0/lab: The young man on the bridge
/entries/e_bridge/archive/1/fields/1/lab: What he hopes to do before sailing
/entries/e_bridge/archive/1/fields/2/tex: The Captain supervises the cargo crossing at the river while the young man takes the customary footpath
/entries/e_bridge/archive/1/fields/3/tex: The novel does not give the Captain foreknowledge of danger or make the young man’s crossing a deliberate act of self-destruction
/entries/e_bridge/archive/1/fields/4/tex: They have just tried to continue living. The accident does not cancel the companionship itself
/entries/e_bridge/archive/2/fields/1/lab: The child’s little object for the night
/entries/e_bridge/archive/2/fields/2/tex: Pio says they will rest on the other side; this small plan for the unwell child is never fulfilled
/entries/e_bridge/archive/2/fields/3/tex: María, Pepita, Esteban, Pio and Jaime perish in the same bridge disaster
/entries/e_bridge/archive/2/fields/4/tex: Their lives can be known more closely without the ultimate cause of the accident becoming a provable answer
